## Comparison — E-Bikes Under $1,500 (verified Sept 5, 2026)

| | **Lectric XPress2 Stratus Cruiser** | **Aventon Soltera 3 ADV** | **Rad Power RadRunner** | **Aventon Soltera 2.5** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Price** | **$1,399** (from $2,122) | $1,499 | $1,499 | **$999** ($200 off) |
| **Motor** | 750W nom / **1310W peak** | 250W nom / 540W peak, 40 Nm | 750W hub, 60 Nm | 540W peak |
| **Battery** | 48V 14Ah ≈ **672 Wh** | 36.9V 9.94Ah = **367 Wh** | 48V 13Ah = **624 Wh** | n/a listed |
| **Claimed range** | up to 60 mi | up to 70 mi | 17–55+ mi | up to 46 mi |
| **Top speed / class** | **28 mph (Class 3)** | 20 mph (Class 1, no throttle) | 20 mph (Class 2, throttle) | 20 mph |
| **Weight / payload** | 330 lb payload | **37 lbs** | 320 lb payload | 46 lbs |
| **Commuter extras** | 80mm susp. fork; **free rack + fenders + spare 672Wh battery ($723 value)** | Belt drive, torque sensor, hydraulic discs, turn signals, IPX6 | Cadence sensor, IPX6, UL 2849/2271 | Shimano 7-speed |
| **Availability** | Preorder — ships week of **Sept 28** | **In stock now** | **Back Order** | In stock now |

*Note: Rad Power's entire remaining lineup (RadWagon, RadRunner Plus/Max, Radster) starts at $1,799 and is over budget.*

## Recommendation: Lectric XPress2 Stratus — $1,399

**Reasoning tied to your 16-mile daily round trip (~80 mi/week):**

1. **Range is a non-issue, permanently.** 672 Wh covers 16 flat miles with ~70% left over. Critically, the current promo includes a **free second 672 Wh battery** — that's ~1,344 Wh total, so you could ride an entire work week without charging. No other bike here comes close on energy-per-dollar.
2. **Class 3 (28 mph) cuts real time off your commute.** On mostly flat roads, this is where speed actually translates to minutes saved — roughly 8–10 min saved each way versus the 20 mph Class 1/2 options. The other three are all capped at 20 mph.
3. **The free rack and fenders are commuter necessities**, not extras. Buying those separately on the Aventon or Rad pushes you to or past $1,600.
4. **It comes in $100 under budget**, leaving room for a helmet and lock.

**Trade-off to be aware of:** it's a preorder shipping the week of **Sept 28** (~3 weeks out).

**If you need a bike this week instead:** the **Aventon Soltera 3 ADV ($1,499, in stock)** is the pick — at 37 lbs with a maintenance-free belt drive, torque sensor and built-in turn signals, it's the nicest bike to actually ride and carry. Its 367 Wh battery is the smallest here, but 16 flat miles is well within a single charge; expect to plug in every other day.

**Budget option:** the **Soltera 2.5 at $999** handles your commute fine and saves $400 — but you give up hydraulic brakes, the belt drive and lights.

I'd steer you away from the **RadRunner**: at $1,499 it's the same price as the far better-equipped Soltera 3, it's back-ordered anyway, and its 17-mile low-end range estimate (throttle-heavy riding) is uncomfortably close to your 16-mile daily requirement.
